aiSummary: I sing and lament the Eye of the Diphyes—the Fire-Eye, Gate-Rending Eye, and Eye of the Great Judge—described as a dread, lidless, circular, bronze-like eye that never dims, burning with coal-white intensity, and perpetually watchful, hanging where no roof beam reaches yet surveying through gaps and barriers. It counts the living, the dying, and the hidden, piercing through stone, metal, and shadow, marking every movement and secret with precision, and dwelling in objects like cauldrons and swords. It is likened to a tyrant in mirrors, a tracker of multitudes, and a net-weaver in thought, pursuing solitude, crowds, and self-deception, with no corner safe from its all-seeing, unyielding gaze. Its presence is felt in winter, in darkness, and in every concealed act, revealing every hidden truth, and it remembers all it has seen, weighing and splitting reality like doors broken by a ram. In dread and despair, the speaker acknowledges that all are exposed to this relentless, all-remembering Eye of Fire, which numbers ten thousand times ten thousand.
title: Hymn 30
